_about: GENERATED by scripts/docs/gen_adsorbent_library.py from library.json and the <key>.json blobs; do not edit. Validated, merged catalogue: each entry is its library.json record plus `recommended` and its serialised adsorbent (`adsorbent`), in the order of docs/adsorbent-library.md.

zeolite-13x.name: Zeolite 13X
zeolite-13x.recommended_reason: Measured by the authors on a named commercial grade (CO2 and N2, 298-348 K, 0-1 bar); the engine's Perez 2019 paper tests check it against VSA experiments. The CO2/CH4/H2 variant has a CO2 fit copied from an earlier paper; the CO2/CH4 variant is a refit of another group's data.

zeolite-5a.name: Zeolite 5A
zeolite-5a.recommended_reason: The only 5A entry measured by its authors (N2, 298-338 K, 0.01-20 bar). For O2 or CO2/CH4 use a variant: the N2/O2 parameters are copied from earlier papers and the CO2/CH4 parameters are a refit of another group's data.

lix.recommended_reason: A fit by Ferre et al. to data measured by Park et al. (2014). The N2/O2 variant's parameters are copied from earlier papers, so it ranks below a refit of measured data.

notes: Water uses the engine kind 'gab' (Eq. 12, Table 5: q_m = 3.51 mmol/g, c = 2.73, k_G = 0.867) in relative humidity with temperature-independent constants (dH_m = dH_C = dH_K = 0), as the authors do (water isotherms at 15, 25 and 35 C collapse in relative humidity). The paper does not state its saturation-pressure correlation (Not stated in source (checked: Sections 2.3.3 and 3.2.2, Eq. 12, Table 5, SI; the paper states only that the vapor pressure sets the temperature dependence)); the engine uses CoolProp. The GAB gives 3.463 mol/kg = 0.986 q_m at x = 0.43, the monolayer point of p. 7170.

CO2 uses the engine kind 'toth_wadst' (Eq. 13): dry site = Table 4, wet site and A = Table 6 (WADST column). The engine has one T_0 for both sites; the paper references the dry site to 308 K (printed as 308, not 308.15) and the wet site to 298.15 K, so T_0 = 308 K and the wet site is re-referenced by the exact relations chi' = chi T0'/T0, q' = q exp(chi - chi'), alpha' = alpha T0/T0', t0' = t0 + alpha - alpha' (T0 = 298.15 K, T0' = 308 K; derived values are marked in the table). The paper's b0 is the affinity at T0 in kPa^-1, the engine's has no reference temperature, so b0_dry = b0 exp(-dH/(R T0)) = 2.96 exp(-77800/(8.314462618 x 308)) 1/Pa = 1.8933e-13 1/Pa; b0_wet = 31 kPa^-1 = 0.031 1/Pa (dH_wet = 0). Stored values: T_0 = 308 K; dry q_inf = 1.17, chi = 0.49, b0 = 1.8933e-13 1/Pa, dH = 77800 J/mol, tau0 = 0.25, alpha = 0.19; wet q_inf = 1.5015 (1.62 exp(2.3 - 2.3760)), chi = 2.3760 (2.3 x 308/298.15), b0 = 0.031 1/Pa, dH = 0, tau0 = 1.1567 (1.0 + 4.9 - 4.7433), alpha = 4.7433 (4.9 x 298.15/308); A = 2.8 mol/kg. Table 6 gives no CI for t0,wet and dH_wet (physical bounds). At zero water loading it is exactly the dry Table 4 isotherm (the dry Toth-2 form, b0 now at infinite temperature instead of at T0). The water weighting uses the actual adsorbed water loading; the paper's fits use the equilibrium loading at the measured RH, which is the same at equilibrium.

WADST overestimates CO2 uptake above about 50 % RH and cannot show the decrease at 10 % RH (Section 3.4); the authors recommend CATSO for this sorbent. The engine has no CATSO kind. CATSO parameters, for reference (Eqs. 14-18, Table 6): dry Toth = Table 4; wet Toth q_s,0,wet 0.60 mol/kg, b0,wet 40 kPa^-1, t0,wet 1.0, dH_wet 0, alpha_wet 6.2, chi_wet 0.2 (T0 = 298.15 K); S = 20 (chosen), K = 2.28, b_H2O = 0.064 (kPa^-1 by dimensional consistency; Not stated in source (checked: Table 6, Eq. 15); the paper gives no unit), x_H2O,m = 0.43; the competitive and collaborative terms use the relative humidity directly.

SI Table S1 prints measured CO2 uptakes at 400 ppm: at 298 K dry 0.48, 10 % RH 0.47, 20 % 0.6, 40 % 0.74, 50 % 0.74, 70 % 0.76, 90 % 0.76 mmol/g; at 308 K dry 0.47, 20 % 0.61, 40 % 0.67, 50 % 0.66. The dry Toth reproduces 0.48 at 298 K (0.4855 mol/kg at 40.5 Pa) but gives 0.406 against 0.47 at 308 K (the b0 CI is about +/-80 %); with the GAB water loading the WADST isotherm gives 0.554 mol/kg at 298.15 K and 20 % RH, and the WADST and CATSO fits are within about 0.05-0.08 mol/kg of the 298 K values.

The water heat is the average isosteric heat of the isotherms (Clausius-Clapeyron, ca. 45 kJ/mol; ca. 59 kJ/mol at zero coverage), not a calorimetric value; the paper gives no uncertainty or data table for it.
The material is an amine-functionalised alumina; no plain activated-alumina source with an engine-supported model was found.
